title: Relativistic Quantum Thermometry in AdS Spacetime via Non-Markovian Temperature Sensing
authors: Anass Hminat, Abdallah Slaoui, Rachid Ahl Laamara
abstract: Quantum thermometry based on single-qubit sensor configurations enables the precise estimation of the temperature of a cosmological Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. In this work, we characterize the achievable estimation accuracy using the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and the associated quantum signal-to-noise ratio. For the first time, we introduce an ancillary Unruh-DeWitt detector between the sensor and the thermal bath, enhancing thermometric sensitivity by channeling temperature-dependent information into the probe qubit's coherence. We examine how detector acceleration in AdS space and the choice of boundary conditions modify the probe's thermal sensitivity. Despite the differing geometries, a unified phenomenology emerges: we characterize the scaling of the QFI with respect to temperature, detector energy gap, spacetime curvature, and interaction time. Finally, we identify optimal state preparation and measurement strategies that maximize the QFI, thereby establishing the fundamental limits of precision for non-Markovian sensing in curved spacetime.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to estimate the temperature of an Anti-de Sitter spacetime using single-qubit sensors. By incorporating an ancillary detector and analyzing non-Markovian effects, the authors derive fundamental limits on measurement precision using the Quantum Fisher Information. The findings show that non-Markovian dynamics can enhance sensing accuracy, particularly at low temperatures.
main_problem: The primary goal is to characterize the fundamental limits of precision for estimating the temperature ($T$) of a cosmological Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime using quantum thermometry.
main_result: The study establishes that non-Markovian dynamics can enhance sensing efficiency, and optimal performance ($	ext{QSNR}$) is achieved in the low-temperature regime by maximizing coherence.
method: The analysis employs quantum estimation theory, utilizing the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to set the ultimate precision bound on temperature estimation.
model_or_system: The system involves a single-qubit sensor interacting with a thermal bath generated by AdS spacetime. Sensitivity is enhanced using an ancillary Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a massless scalar field.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Quantum Signal-to-Noise Ratio (QSNR), and the information-flow measure ($N$) characterizing non-Markovianity.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), spacetime curvature ($\ell$), detector acceleration ($a$), coupling constant ($\kappa$), and interaction time ($t$).
main_assumptions: The local quantum estimation framework assumes prior, coarse knowledge of the parameter value $T$. The analysis distinguishes between transient effects and long-time stationary values.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes mention Figure 9 showing QSNR dependence on temperature).
paper_structure: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum metrology in curved spacetime, deriving the QFI using detector response functions calculated from Wightman two-point functions specific to AdS space. It then analyzes how non-Markovian dynamics modify this estimation bound.
why_interesting: It directly addresses open quantum systems and thermalization processes (non-Markovianity) within a curved spacetime background, which is highly relevant for understanding realistic quantum sensing in cosmology or high-energy physics settings.
